New in JMIR Nursing: From Academic Integrity to Professional Formation in Generative AI–Supported Nursing Education: Integrative Review #NursingEducation #GenerativeAI #AcademicIntegrity #ClinicalPractice #AIinHealthcare

external.description: Background: The rapid integration of generative AI (GenAI) into #nursing education has prompted widespread concern about academic integrity and assessment validity. However, this dominant discourse may obscure a more fundamental challenge: preparing #nursing students for clinical practice environments where AI already mediates triage, diagnostics, documentation, and clinical decision-making. Objective: This integrative review examines how GenAI is conceptualized within the #nursing education literature and investigates the extent to which current discourse addresses professional formation rather than academic compliance. Methods: Following Whittemore and Knafl’s integrative review methodology, a systematic search of PubMed, Google Scholar, and SciSpace (Typeset) was conducted for literature published between January 2022 and February 2026. Two reviewers independently screened 456 records, with 119 papers meeting the inclusion criteria. The methodological quality of empirical studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Corpus-level descriptive mapping quantified dominant themes and conceptual patterns, while an interpretive synthesis examined how GenAI was framed and the extent to which professional formation elements, including identity, moral agency, and clinical judgment, were addressed. Results: Of the 119 unique studies analyzed, 84% (n=100) predominantly framed GenAI as a content-generation tool and academic integrity threat. Only 35.3% (n=42) conceptualized AI as a pedagogical tool, and a critical gap was identified in professional formation: identity formation was addressed in only 10% (n=12) of papers and moral agency in just 5% (n=6). Explicit acknowledgment that AI already routinely mediates frontline clinical decisions (eg, sepsis alerts and fall risk algorithms) in current practice settings was notably absent. The discourse emphasizes governance and faculty literacy, but sustained curricula addressing #nurse identity in AI-mediated care remain underdeveloped. Conclusions: Current #nursing education discourse predominantly frames AI as a writing tool and an academic integrity concern, failing to prepare students for the algorithmic practice environments they will inhabit. Nursing education must reframe AI as a professional formation issue, explicitly addressing how algorithms reshape clinical judgment, moral agency, and professional identity.
external.title: From Academic Integrity to Professional Formation in Generative AI–Supported Nursing Education: Integrative Review

record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: An Exceptional Mobility Group Among Older Adults: #Protocol for the Super Movers #Study

external.description: Background: Gait dysfunction is a preclinical marker of Alzheimer disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD), often emerging years before clinical diagnosis. While much of the existing literature has focused on the pathological mechanisms driving motor and cognitive decline, the neural and biological substrates that confer resilience against such decline remain poorly understood. Individuals who maintain exceptional gait performance into advanced age, termed Super Movers, represent a unique phenotype of resilient aging. Understanding the biological profile of these individuals offers a unique and largely untapped window into the mechanisms underlying healthy aging and resilience to dementia. Objective: This #Study aims to identify the structural, functional, neurophysiological, and molecular brain characteristics that distinguish older adults with exceptional mobility from their usual and slow-moving peers, and to determine whether these characteristics predict cognitive and physical decline over time. We hypothesize that the interplay between protective and pathological mechanisms in aging gives rise to structural, functional, neurophysiological, and molecular brain changes that manifest along a continuum from resilient gait to gait dysfunction. Methods: We aim to enroll 350 adults aged 65 years and older from community and clinic settings. Participants will be classified by gait speed into fast, usual, and slow movers using age- and sex-specific thresholds; fast movers aged 80 years and older will be designated as Super Movers. All participants will undergo comprehensive assessments at baseline, including brain imaging, mobile electroencephalogram (EEG) recorded during walking, multisensory integration (MSI), comprehensive blood profiling, blood-based markers of neurodegeneration, epigenetic and proteomic aging clocks, and detailed cognitive testing. Follow-up assessments will be conducted annually in person and every 6 months by telephone. Results: This #Study was funded by the National Institute on Aging (R01AG089096; PI: Joe Verghese) and has received Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval from Stony Brook University. Enrollment is currently underway. Conclusions: Fast and Super Movers are expected to demonstrate distinct neural substrates, EEG activation signatures, and favorable biomarker profiles relative to usual and slow movers. By shifting the scientific focus from the biology of gait decline toward the biology of gait resilience, this #Protocol is uniquely positioned to advance our understanding of healthy aging and inform novel strategies for dementia prevention. International Registered Report Identifier (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/104520

record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Real-World Implementation and Evaluation of a #Digital Health Platform for Children Living With Type 1 #Diabetes: #Protocol for a Real-World Implementation #Study

external.description: Background: #Digital platforms that integrate continuous glucose monitoring, patient-generated data, and clinical decision support could enable more proactive pediatric type 1 #Diabetes (T1D) care. Sustained uptake of #Digital platforms in routine practice is limited, and the evidence of effectiveness is mixed. Implementation science approaches are needed to clarify how context, workflows, and strategies shape adoption and outcomes. Haibu #Diabetes is a new platform that brings together ##Wearable, patient-reported, and clinical #Diabetes data to generate personalized, data-driven insights for patients and clinicians. Objective: This #Study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and implementation processes of Haibu #Diabetes in routine pediatric T1D care using a hybrid design guided by an Implementation #Research Logic Model. Methods: We will conduct a nonrandomized, quasi-experimental, type 2 hybrid implementation-effectiveness trial at a hospital that provides multidisciplinary pediatric #Diabetes care. Youth aged 3 to less than 18 years with T1D and caregivers will be onboarded to Haibu #Diabetes as part of routine workflows; health care providers will use a clinician dashboard to review data, assign tasks/forms, and communicate asynchronously. Effectiveness analyses will compare Haibu #Diabetes users to a matched control group drawn from the BC Pediatric #Diabetes Registry. Effectiveness outcomes are hemoglobin A, continuous glucose monitoring device-derived time in range over 12 months, and #Diabetes self-care behaviors. Implementation outcomes will be assessed using mixed methods guided by an Implementation #Research Logic Model that links determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes. These outcomes will include reach, adoption, feasibility, acceptability, and maintenance. Health care improvement outcomes will include patient and caregiver experience, clinician experience, and operational workflow indicators. Results: #Study funding commenced in January 2023. Patient recruitment began in September 2026, and 7 participants had consented as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by December 2027, with analysis to follow. #Study findings are expected to be published in summer 2028. Conclusions: This trial will generate real-world evidence on both effectiveness and the conditions required to implement and sustain a data-integrating #Digital platform in pediatric T1D care, informing scale-up and optimization. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07712809; https://clinicaltrials.gov/#Study/NCT07712809 International Registered Report Identifier (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107634
